experiments.scope: Reduced event on the selected Orchard Poseidon target at its own round count: the first 14 bits of the big-endian reading of the 32-byte digest agree for two distinct canonical messages. One birthday search per organizer trial over fresh inputs from the trial seed. No full collision is expected or claimed.
experiments.hypothesis: A search of at most 1200 fresh inputs returns a pair whose digests agree on those 14 bits in every trial, as a random 14-bit function would. Checks the digest of the selected target at one reduced width; it says nothing about the full-width map, the cost or the success probability.

experiments.scope: Reduced event on the selected Orchard Poseidon target at its own round count, on the line construction of proof.md section 2: the first 6 bits of the big-endian reading of the 32-byte digest agree for two distinct canonical messages that are the antipodal points W = c+s and W = c-s about a centre c of the line j = 0 of the first two rounds. One scan of the pairs s = 1, ..., 150 per organizer trial, the centre from the trial seed. No full collision is expected or claimed.
experiments.hypothesis: The digest difference F(c+s) - F(c-s) = 2 s g_c(s^2) of the antipodal points behaves as a random function of s at width 6: a trial returns a pair with probability 1-(1-2^-6)^150 = 0.9058, about 232 of the 256 trials. Checks the digest of the selected target on the antipodal line pairs of the attack at one reduced width; it says nothing about the full-width map, the cost or the success probability.

experiments.scope: Euclidean-normality test of the attack's own construction at reduced depth, on the selected Orchard Poseidon target: for a centre c from the trial seed, the program builds the digest polynomial of the first 4 rounds of the selected permutation on the line j = 0 of proof.md section 2 (full rounds 0-3 and partial rounds 4..3, coordinate 0, same constants and MDS; degree 25), its monic odd part g_c about c (degree m = 12), R_c = x^((p-1)/2) mod g_c, and the complete Euclidean remainder sequence of (g_c, R_c - 1), exactly over F_p. The first 256 trials are computed (the sandbox budget); the other trials return two nulls. When the trial's sequence is normal (every quotient of degree 1 down to the gcd, proof.md 4.4 and 6.3) the program returns two distinct canonical messages of the selected target whose digests agree on the first 6 bits, found by a short search of the points c + s on the line; otherwise two nulls. The returned pair is the witness that the trial was computed and found normal; the measurement is the normality check (proof.md 9.5 and 10.5.1), whose counts are reported as observations. No full collision is expected or claimed.
experiments.hypothesis: Every computed sequence is normal, so exactly 256 of the 256 trials return a pair (the first 256); the gcd of (g_c, R_c - 1) has positive degree in about 40% of them (a usable root, E[k] about 1/2). Supports the premise H-NORMAL of proof.md 9.5 at degree 25 (m = 12) under trusted execution; it says nothing about the scale m = 381,469,726,562 of the claim, nor about the cost or the success probability.
